tagline: Horsepower, heritage, and the endless argument about manual gearboxes.
why: Cars are the one hobby almost everyone has an opinion on. Car people bond over performance, design, nostalgia for the cars they grew up with, and big debates about where things are going: electric vs petrol, screens vs buttons, automatic vs manual. In Hong Kong cars are also a status statement because owning one is so expensive. You don't need to know engineering, just the vocabulary and the personalities of the brands.

essentials.title: Engines in plain words
essentials.body: People talk about cylinders (four, six, V8, V12), turbocharged vs naturally aspirated, and horsepower (top-end power) vs torque (pulling force).

essentials.title: Which wheels drive
essentials.body: FWD (front-wheel drive) is practical, RWD (rear-wheel drive) is the enthusiast's favourite, AWD (all-wheel drive) grips best in bad weather.

essentials.title: Powertrains
essentials.body: Petrol, diesel, hybrid (petrol plus battery), plug-in hybrid and fully electric (EV). Hybrids are booming as a middle ground.

essentials.title: Car cultures
essentials.body: JDM (Japanese), Euro (German and Italian), American muscle, off-road, exotics and supercars, EV fans. People usually belong to one tribe.

essentials.title: Brands have personalities
essentials.body: Porsche is precision, Ferrari is passion, Toyota is reliability, BMW is 'the ultimate driving machine', Mercedes is luxury, Tesla is tech, Volvo is safety.

essentials.title: Body styles
essentials.body: Saloon (sedan), hatchback, estate (wagon), coupe, convertible, SUV, MPV (people carrier). SUVs now dominate sales worldwide.

essentials.title: Everything is changing
essentials.body: Electrification, Chinese brands going global, and software-heavy cars are the big shifts car people talk about.

jargon.meaning: Horsepower is how fast you can go; torque is the shove you feel when you accelerate.
Naturally aspirated: no turbo. Purists love the sound and instant response.
A device that forces more air into the engine for more power from a smaller engine.
Seconds to go from 0 to 100 km/h (0-60 mph in the US). The universal bragging number.
A gearbox with a clutch pedal you shift yourself. Increasingly rare and beloved.
Dual-clutch transmission: a lightning-fast automatic used in many performance cars.
Japanese Domestic Market: Japanese cars and the culture around them, like Supras and Skylines.
Oversteer: the rear slides out. Understeer: the front won't turn as much as you want.
The car someone uses every day, as opposed to a weekend toy.
A car that looks ordinary but is secretly very fast.
A classic car restored with modern parts, like a 1960s body with a modern engine.
An event where regular people drive their own cars on a race track.
EV owners' fear of running out of charge.
Plug-in hybrid: can drive a short distance on electricity, then uses petrol.
Deliberately sliding a car sideways through corners, a Japanese-born motorsport.
Supercars are Ferraris and Lamborghinis; hypercars are the million-dollar-plus tier like Bugatti.

names.name: Porsche
names.what: The 911 has been made since 1964 and is the benchmark sports car. The Cayenne SUV pays the bills.

names.name: Ferrari
names.what: Italian supercars, red paint and the prancing horse. Owners famously must be 'approved' for some models.

names.name: Toyota
names.what: The world's biggest carmaker. Bulletproof reliability, plus the Supra, GR Yaris and Land Cruiser for enthusiasts. Its Alphard van is a status symbol in Asia.

names.name: Tesla
names.what: Made electric cars cool. Elon Musk's company is as much talked about for politics and stock price as cars.

names.name: BYD
names.what: China's EV giant, which sold more pure electric cars than Tesla worldwide in 2025.

names.name: Xiaomi
names.what: The phone maker's SU7 electric car became a hit in China in 2024, followed by the YU7 SUV.

names.name: BMW M
names.what: BMW's performance division. M3 and M5 are icons of the fast saloon.

names.name: Mercedes-Benz
names.what: The S-Class is the benchmark luxury car; the G-Wagen is a celebrity favourite.

names.name: Mazda MX-5 Miata
names.what: The best-selling two-seat roadster ever. The default answer to 'what fun cheap car should I buy?'

names.name: Ford Mustang
names.what: The original pony car (1964) and the face of American muscle.

names.name: Lamborghini
names.what: Wild, wedge-shaped supercars and Ferrari's flashier rival.

names.name: Rolls-Royce
names.what: The ultimate luxury car, owned by BMW. A common sight outside Hong Kong hotels.

names.name: Jeremy Clarkson
names.what: Former Top Gear and The Grand Tour host, the most famous car TV personality.

names.name: Nissan Skyline GT-R
names.what: 'Godzilla', the JDM legend from Gran Turismo and Fast & Furious.

timeline.event: Karl Benz patents the first practical car.
Ford's Model T makes cars affordable for ordinary families.
Ford Mustang launches the pony car era; Porsche 911 goes on sale.
The oil crisis pushes buyers toward small, efficient Japanese cars.
Japan's golden era: Miata, NSX, Supra, Skyline GT-R.
The Toyota Prius, the first mass-market hybrid.
The Fast and the Furious makes JDM tuning culture global.
Top Gear relaunches and becomes the world's biggest car show.
The Tesla Model S proves electric cars can be desirable.
EV push, then a slowdown and a hybrid comeback; Chinese brands surge.

now.headline: EV slowdown, hybrid comeback
now.detail: Electric car growth slowed in the US and Europe, and hybrids (Toyota's long-time bet) are booming.

now.headline: China is the new powerhouse
now.detail: BYD, Xiaomi, Zeekr and others build impressive, cheaper EVs. Tariffs keep many out of the US and Europe charges extra duties.

now.headline: Tesla's tough patch
now.detail: Sales fell in several markets, and people debate whether it's a car company or a robotaxi and AI bet.

now.headline: Screens vs buttons
now.detail: Many drivers and safety groups are pushing back on touchscreens for basic controls; some brands are bringing buttons back.

now.headline: Self-driving
now.detail: Robotaxis from Waymo and Chinese firms like Baidu's Apollo Go are spreading, and people argue about when it'll be normal.

now.headline: Porsche and others retreat on EVs
now.detail: Several luxury brands slowed EV plans and kept petrol engines longer than promised.

local.headline: Owning a car is a luxury
local.detail: Hong Kong's first registration tax can more than double a car's price, and a parking space can cost more than a flat elsewhere.

local.headline: Tesla and BYD everywhere
local.detail: EV tax incentives made Hong Kong one of the world's most electric car markets. BYD has grown fast.

local.headline: Status cars
local.detail: Toyota Alphard vans with drivers, Mercedes S-Class, Rolls-Royces and Ferraris are common sights in Central.

local.headline: Northbound Travel
local.detail: Since 2023 Hong Kong private cars can drive into Guangdong via the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge, making weekend road trips popular.

local.headline: Drive on the left
local.detail: Hong Kong drives on the left with right-hand-drive cars, like the UK and Japan, unlike the mainland.

debates.question: Manual or automatic?
debates.sides: Automatics are faster now; manual fans say driving is about involvement, not lap times.

debates.question: Electric or petrol?
debates.sides: EVs are quick and cheap to run; critics cite charging, range and price, and miss the sound.

debates.question: Are Chinese cars now as good as Japanese and German ones?
debates.sides: Many reviewers say yes on tech and value; sceptics question long-term reliability and resale.

debates.question: Are modern cars too big?
debates.sides: SUVs keep growing. Fans like the space; critics point to safety and parking.

debates.question: JDM vs Euro
debates.sides: Japanese cars for reliability and tuning; German and Italian for prestige and driving feel.

sayThis.say: The Miata is always the answer.
sayThis.why: A beloved in-joke among car people.
Enthusiasts appreciate the question even if the answer is no.
Shows you get the appeal of understated performance.

sayThis.say: Chinese EVs have come a long way.

avoid: Confidently quoting specs you aren't sure of. Car people will check.
Dismissing someone's car as 'just a car'.
Asking how much someone's car or parking space cost.

quiz.explain: The rear wheels drive the car, which enthusiasts tend to prefer.

deep.title: Marque by marque
deep.intro: Each brand's legends and the cars that set auction records.

groups.name: Ferrari
groups.intro: Maranello, Italy. Red, the prancing horse, and limited production so demand always beats supply.

items.name: Ferrari 250 GTO
items.what: 36 built in 1962-64 for racing. The most valuable Ferrari and the blue-chip collector car.
items.value: US$51.7m at auction (RM Sotheby's, 2023); private sales reportedly about US$70m

items.name: Ferrari F40
items.what: 1987, the last car Enzo Ferrari approved: twin-turbo, huge wing, no comfort at all.

items.name: Ferrari Enzo
items.what: 2002 hypercar named after the founder; 400 made.

items.name: LaFerrari
items.what: 2013 hybrid hypercar, part of the 'holy trinity' with the McLaren P1 and Porsche 918.

items.name: Ferrari Purosangue
items.what: Ferrari's first four-door, four-seat car (2022). Don't call it an SUV in front of a Ferrari owner.

groups.name: Porsche
groups.intro: Stuttgart. Precision engineering, and the 911 has kept its shape for 60 years.

items.name: Porsche 911
items.what: The rear-engined icon since 1963. Fans name generations by code: 964, 993 (last air-cooled), 997, 992.

items.name: 911 GT3 / GT3 RS
items.what: Track-focused 911s with high-revving engines and big wings; the enthusiast's choice.

items.name: Porsche 959
items.what: 1986 technological marvel with four-wheel drive; Bill Gates famously owned one.

items.name: Carrera GT
items.what: V10 supercar from 2004 with a manual gearbox; feared and adored.

items.name: Taycan
items.what: Porsche's electric saloon, a familiar sight in Hong Kong.

groups.name: Lamborghini
groups.intro: Sant'Agata, Italy, owned by VW Group via Audi. Wild shapes, V12s and scissor doors.

items.name: Miura
items.what: 1966, the first mid-engined supercar. Many say the most beautiful car ever.

items.name: Countach
items.what: 1974 wedge with scissor doors; the bedroom-poster car of the 80s.

items.name: Aventador
items.what: The 2011-2022 V12 flagship.

items.name: Revuelto
items.what: 2023 V12 plug-in hybrid flagship.

items.name: Urus
items.what: The SUV that pays the bills: Lamborghini's best-seller.

items.name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé
items.what: One of two road-going versions of a 1955 racing car, named after its engineer.
items.value: €135m (RM Sotheby's private auction, 2022): most expensive car ever sold

items.name: McLaren F1
items.what: 1992, three seats with the driver in the middle, gold foil in the engine bay; the fastest car of its era.

items.name: Bugatti Chiron
items.what: 1,500 hp, over 400 km/h. Bugatti is now part of Bugatti Rimac.

items.name: Rolls-Royce Boat Tail
items.what: Bespoke coachbuilt cars with a yacht-style rear deck; reportedly about US$28m each.

items.name: Aston Martin DB5
items.what: James Bond's car from Goldfinger (1964).

items.name: Rolls-Royce Phantom
items.what: The flagship limousine with the Spirit of Ecstasy and rear-hinged 'coach' doors.

items.name: Rolls-Royce Cullinan
items.what: The Rolls SUV, named after the largest diamond ever found.

items.name: Mercedes-Benz G-Class
items.what: The square off-roader turned status symbol; an electric version arrived in 2024.

items.name: Toyota Alphard
items.what: The boxy luxury MPV that shuttles Hong Kong's executives and celebrities.

items.name: Tesla Model Y
items.what: For years the world's best-selling car of any kind; everywhere in Hong Kong.

items.name: BYD and Xiaomi SU7
items.what: China's EV giants: BYD outsells Tesla globally; Xiaomi's SU7 saloon sold out in minutes.
